title: seller-sprint-empathy-mapping-and-risk-scripts-draft
content:
Purpose: a compact, seller-facing sprint kit to surface customer empathy, map pilot risks, and give tight objection scripts and micro-decks for 10–15 minute demos. Draft status: intentionally terse — use as quick reference in calls and for SDR/SE handoffs.

Audience: integration SEs, account execs, platform sellers, pilot owners. Primary goals: qualify latency/cost sensitivity, align on SLOs, secure a pilot scope that demonstrates value while keeping cost bounded.

Top-level flow (60 mins seller sprint):
- 0–5m: Quick rapport + expected outcomes (set the clock)
- 5–15m: Empathy mapping Qs (technical constraints, compliance, data flow)
- 15–30m: Show 3-slide micro-deck (value hooks, quick demo, safety/fallback)
- 30–40m: Pilot mechanics (traffic, routing, fallbacks, success metrics)
- 40–55m: Objections & risk table — negotiate mitigations
- 55–60m: Next steps — commit to a single test (e.g., 1 endpoint, 10k tokens/day for 2 weeks)

Empathy mapping (templates sellers can use live in call):
- Persona: Integration Architect / Platform Engineer / Product Manager
- What keeps them up at night? (prompt seller to ask)
  - "What are the worst-case outcomes if inference is slow or inconsistent?"
  - "Who owns downstream retries or user-facing error handling?"
- Constraints: network egress, internal PKI/KMS, audit/retention windows, PII handling
- Success signals (short, measurable): median latency < 200ms, 99th < 800ms, accuracy metric on prompt set >= baseline, cost < $X/1000 tokens
- Decision-makers and approvers: security, legal, infra, product — confirm names/emails

Quick micro-deck outline (3 slides, speaker notes):
- Slide A: Value thread in one sentence + 2 bullets of business outcome (e.g., "Reduce support triage time by X% / Increase recommendations CTR by Y%")
  - Speaker note: start with a concrete customer vignette that matches their industry (e.g., "One of our platform customers reduced agent handle time by 18% using a cached reranking flow")
- Slide B: Architecture sketch (client -> router policy -> model variants -> fallback) + clear SLO lanes (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
  - Speaker note: emphasize routing policies (latency-first vs cost-first) and default fallback to smaller quantized model for spikes
- Slide C: Pilot ask + success metrics + quick rollback plan
  - Speaker note: make the ask tiny (1 endpoint, 2-week test, explicit traffic slice) and include a rollback criterion (error rate > 3% for 12h triggers halt)

Objection scripts (concise, role-targeted)
- Objection: "This sounds expensive at scale."
  - Reply: "Agreed — we design the pilot to show the signal with minimal spend. Start with a synthetic 5–10% sample and use prefix caching/batching. If signals are positive, we can propose quantization and reserved pools to bring unit cost down before scaling."
- Objection: "We can't send data off-prem."
  - Reply: "We support Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) and can run an air-gapped eval. For the pilot, a VPC private control plane with customer-managed KMS is typical; I'll loop in our private-deployments SE to scope network steps."
- Objection: "We need a documented SLA before we ship anything."
  - Reply: "For pilots we provide operational playbooks and a canary rollback policy. SLA negotiations happen in parallel — we can still run a low-risk pilot with a defined escalation path. I can attach our standard pilot SLA template."

Risk table (simple columns: Risk, Likelihood, Impact, Mitigation (pilot-stage)) — sellers: read aloud and confirm alignment
- Risk: Peak token spend > forecast; Likelihood: medium; Impact: billing surprise; Mitigation: hard quota + alert + automatic throttling to fallbacks
- Risk: Model regression on critical prompt set; Likelihood: low; Impact: customer-facing degradation; Mitigation: baseline prompt eval + gated rollout + rollback threshold
- Risk: Network egress policy / firewall blocks; Likelihood: medium; Impact: pilot blocked; Mitigation: pre-call checklist with infra owner, IP allowlist, VPC peering template

Pre-call checklist (copyable):
- Confirm attendees: infra owner + product + 1 exec sponsor
- Confirm environment: sandbox API key or private endpoint details
- Confirm dataset: 10–50 representative prompts (redact PII)
- Confirm evaluation metrics and where to post results
- Bring a fallback play (e.g., smaller model, cached responses)

Playbook snippets sellers can paste into follow-up email (two options)
- Short follow-up: "Thanks — attached is the pilot scope: 2-week test, 1 endpoint, sample traffic 5–10%, baseline prompts attached. We'll instrument latency & accuracy dashboards and set a pause rule for spend. Next sync: Thu +7 days to review early metrics."
- Detailed ops follow-up: bullet list with contact names, technical steps to enable allowlist, sample cURL for endpoint, expected JSON schema, rollback rules, monitoring links

Pilot handshake — minimal config (technical template):
- Endpoint: hosted.redwood.example/pilot/{customer-id}
- Token budget: 10k tokens/day (soft) with hard cap at 20k/day
- Routing policy: latency-first for prod slice, cost-first for background rerank slice
- Monitoring: metric names (latency_median_ms, error_rate_pct, token_count)
- Alert thresholds: error_rate_pct > 3% sustained > 10min, token_count > 80% of soft budget

Examples: customer vignettes to swap into live calls (short):
- Retail search: built-in caching of session prefix reduced server tokens by 60% while improving relevance scoring accuracy 11% — cost went down, query quality up
- Internal knowledge base: private deployment enabled a regulated customer to run a full pilot inside their VPC; they approved a Dedicated capacity contract after the trial

Open questions / TODOs (for docs owners):
- Add a one-click slide PDF with the 3-slide micro-deck. (who: design)
- Convert the pre-call checklist into a shared doc that populates meeting invites (who: SE ops)
- Build a tiny SLO-simulator spreadsheet for sellers to input traffic and cost assumptions (who: product-marketing)

Notes to self (raw):
- Keep scripts < 20 words per objection — people read quickly in call transcripts
- Emphasize rollback criteria early; reduces procurement friction
- Consider a one-paragraph legal blurb we can append to follow-ups about data handling (for customers who ask for immediate answer)

Appendix: quick cURL sample (for technical follow-up) — paste-friendly
- Example: curl -X POST https://hosted.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <pilot-key>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"rwd-small-qa","input":"<sample prompt>"}'

End of draft — thumbs-up if helpful. Use liberally and iterate.
